summary: This work solves the time-optimal qubit reset problem for frequency-tunable superconducting qubits coupled to a structured environment by applying Pontryagin's minimum principle to derive an optimal switch–restore–switch control sequence. For representative environmental spectra, the scheme achieves reset times as short as 20 ns with fidelity $10^{-5}$, about 40% of typical two-qubit gate times, while exploiting spectral structure as a practical resource.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity reset is critical for qubit reuse in NISQ processors where logical qubit counts exceed available hardware, but achieving rapid reset conflicts with the weak decoherence required for high-fidelity gates. The time-optimal reset strategy under realistic spectral and control constraints remains unclear.
method: We formulate reset as an optimal control problem where the tunable qubit frequency $\omega(t)$ minimizes the restoring duration $\tau_{st}$ subject to the Lindblad dynamics $\dot{p}_e = -\Gamma(\omega)(p_e - p_e^{\mathrm{eq}}(\omega))$ and frequency path constraints $\omega(t) \in [\omega_{\min}, \omega_{\max}]$. Pontryagin's principle yields an algebraic optimality condition that the restoring frequency satisfies $\omega^*(p_e) = \arg\max_{\omega} \Gamma(\omega)(p_e - p_e^{\mathrm{eq}}(\omega))$, enabling time-local control.
result: For four representative superconducting qubit environments (Lorentzian, protected, mixed, and Josephson quantum filter spectra), the total reset time including switching is $T_{\mathrm{reset}} = 2\tau_{sw} + \tau_{st} \sim 20$ ns (prot spectrum) versus $\gtrsim 100$ ns for existing active schemes, with reset precision $\epsilon = 10^{-5}$. For high-contrast spectra, the scheme reduces extra thermodynamic work below the constant-decoherence bound, and fidelity exceeds 99.999% over substantial experimental deviations.
